findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so the caller must be both. That does not match the variable name or the bookings UI, which treats team admin and owner as alternative managers (isUserTeamAdminOrOwner). A team admin who is not an owner is always FORBIDDEN; if those helpers treat ADMIN and OWNER as distinct membership roles, owners are forbidden too. Team managers will see Add guests on a team booking and the mutation will reject them. Use ||, and do not call either helper with teamId 0 when eventType.teamId is null.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the actor and is not rolled back
findings.body: Attendees are inserted with createMany before updateCalendarAttendees. The EventManager is then built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), while booking.user (including credentials) was loaded and never used. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the update targets that person's calendars, not the host calendar that owns the event, so the real event's attendee list is not updated or the call throws. The throw is outside any transaction and outside the email try/catch, so the mutation errors after the rows are committed. A retry then filters those emails as already present and fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid, leaving the booking, calendars, and notifications permanently out of sync. Use the booking host's credentials and roll back the insert if the calendar update fails.

findings.title: Cancelled and rejected bookings can be re-invited
findings.body: Nothing checks booking.status before creating attendees and sending mail. addGuests is only authedProcedure plus the handler's role check, so an organizer, attendee, or permitted team member can call it for a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking even though the list UI hides the action. The new organizer and attendee emails attach an ICS REQUEST with status CONFIRMED, which can put the meeting back on calendars and re-send the video link for a meeting that was declined or cancelled. Gate the update on ACCEPTED (or another explicit allow-list) before writing attendees.

findings.title: Seated events ignore capacity and seat records
findings.body: createMany inserts Attendee rows without checking seatsPerTimeSlot (the same handler later copies that field onto the calendar payload) and without creating BookingSeat rows. Seat availability and payment are based on seat count, so these extra attendees can exceed the cap, receive the meeting link without a paid seat, and are invisible to seat cancel/reschedule flows that use seatsReferences. The emails also include the full attendee list, which leaks other people when seatsShowAttendees is false. Reject addGuests for seated event types, or enforce remaining capacity and create the matching seat records.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and silent
findings.body: uniqueGuests keeps a guest unless guest === attendee.email and unless blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest). The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the input is not lowercased or trimmed, so BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is bypassed by changing case. The same address can also be stored twice (User@x.com vs user@x.com), and duplicates inside the guests array are not removed, so one request can insert the same attendee twice. Filtered addresses are dropped with no per-email error: if any other address remains, the handler returns success and the UI says guests were added; if every address is filtered out, the error is emails_must_be_unique_valid, which is wrong for a blacklist hit. Normalize before compare, dedupe the input, exclude the organizer address, and reject blocked emails instead of skipping them.

findings.title: Guest list has no maximum length
findings.body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no min or max. Anyone the handler allows, including any attendee on the booking, can submit thousands of addresses in one call. Each new address becomes an Attendee row, and sendAddGuestsEmails sends a full booking message (location and video link included) to every attendee. That is an unbounded write and a meeting-link spam path with no limit on this procedure. Cap the array in ZAddGuestsInputSchema and reject an empty list.

findings.title: Emails use the raw guest list and hide send failures
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests input, not uniqueGuests. In email-manager, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new confirmation plus ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting someone already on the booking therefore pushes a second confirmed invite to them, while addresses that were filtered out still affect that branch. The call is wrapped in a try/catch that only console.log's a static string and then returns { message: "Guests added" }, so the dialog shows success even when nobody was notified. Pass only the addresses actually inserted, and log or surface the real send error.

findings.title: disableGuests on the event type is ignored
findings.body: eventType is included on the booking but disableGuests is never read. The normal booking flow refuses additional guests when that flag is set; this mutation still creates Attendee rows and emails them the meeting details. Because the permission check also allows any existing attendee, a guest on a no-guests event type can invite arbitrary people after the fact. Reject the request when booking.eventType.disableGuests is true.

findings.title: Add-guest mail ignores standard-email disable flags
findings.body: sendLocationChangeEmails and the other send helpers in this file skip host or attendee mail when event-type metadata has disableStandardEmails. sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team.members entry, and every attendee, and addGuestsHandler never passes eventType.metadata. Event types configured to suppress standard emails still get guest-added messages and ICS attachments, bypassing workflow-only notification settings. Apply the same host and attendee disable checks here.

findings.title: Calendar payload omits team, so co-hosts are skipped
findings.body: The CalendarEvent built for updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails never sets team. sendAddGuestsEmails only notifies other hosts when calendarEvent.team.members is present, so that loop is dead for this caller. Collective and round-robin co-hosts get no guest-added email or ICS, and destinationCalendar falls back to a single booking.user calendar, so their calendars are not updated either. Populate team the same way the other booking email builders do before calling EventManager and sendAddGuestsEmails.

findings.title: No tests for addGuests authorization or side effects
findings.body: The new mutation decides who may add guests, how emails are filtered, and whether cancelled, seated, or disableGuests bookings are writable, but the PR adds no handler or router tests. The admin&&owner check, case-sensitive blacklist bypass, and cancelled-booking ICS path would ship unnoticed. Cover organizer, team admin, team owner, unrelated user, duplicate and blacklisted emails, seated event types, and non-ACCEPTED statuses.
